text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Pope John Paul II will celebrate multi-ethnicity in Bosnia and his visit is devoted to all people and all religions, Colum Murphy, spokesman to the Office of the High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt, told a news conference.

- Bosnia's joint cabinet failed to reach consensus on the agenda and to discuss a four million German Marks donation for reconstruction of Bosnia parliament's building approved by the World Bank and the European Union.

- Haris Silajdzic, Moslem co-chairman of Bosnia's Council of Ministers, said customs policy and foreign trade law, which were agreed on government's previous session, were based on false interpretation and violated the Constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina.
- Joint police forces in the divided town of Mostar are due to start patroling together on Friday afternoon.
- The OSCE's Media Expert Commission (MEC), charged with monitoring local media, released a set of rules and regulations for media during the upcoming local polls in mid-September.
- Bosnia's opposition leader Muhamed Filipovic thinks the Dayton peace agreement was merely an instrument to end the war in Bosnia.

- The Norwegian Red Cross completed a six month-long reconstruction of a psychiatric hospital in Sokolac in the Serb Republic (30 km east of Sarajevo), the International Committee of Red Cross (ICRC) says in a press release.
- German province Bavaria is likely to deport 15 Bosnian refugees from Munich to Bosnia on Friday, Bosnian vice-consul in Munich says.
- 15,000 Bosnian refugees expelled from Bosnian Serb-held Bijeljina and Janja are due to return soon from Berlin to Bosnia, newspaper says.
- Federation of International Football Associations (FIFA) gave the match between Bosnia and Greece highest rating, newspaper quotes FIFA'a official as saying.

- Newly appointed international supervisor for the disputed town of Brcko Bill Farrand starts his first working day on April 7, sources close to the Office of the High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, told newspaper. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
